sub_area: Test fixture helper functions for blog/category/blogger doctypes; no test class
rationale: This file contains only helper functions (create_test_blog_post, setup_for_tests, etc.) used by other test files; there is no TestCase class and nothing is exercised over HTTP. Ferro has no obligation here.

sub_area: Hook registry: app_name, doc_events, override_doctype_class, has_permission hook, ignore_links_on_delete, fixture export prefix
rationale: All tests call frappe.* in-process and test the Python hook dispatch mechanism; ferro has no hook registry, no Python event system, and no fixture-export feature — this is intentionally absent from the pure-Rust build.

sub_area: Custom auth_hook: sets user via Authorization Bearer token through HTTP
rationale: TestAPIHooks sends a real HTTP request and expects a custom auth_hook to run (setting the user from a custom token prefix); ferro's auth.rs has no hook dispatch and would ignore this custom hook, returning a different user. Partial fidelity is acceptable given the hook system is intentionally absent.

sub_area: linked_with: references across doctypes by link/dynamic-link fields, submitted linked docs, delete integrity, reserved SQL keyword fieldnames
rationale: Tests call frappe.desk.form.linked_with Python functions directly (no HTTP); the linked_with subsystem is not implemented in ferro and is not part of its REST surface, so ferro has no obligation here.

sub_area: List View Settings CRUD and get_group_by_count / reportview.get() with comment count
rationale: Tests call frappe.db and frappe.desk.reportview.get() in-process; the reportview.get path (get_list with filters, group-by) encodes ORM semantics that ferro reimplements via orm.rs, but the specific List View Settings and group_by_count features are not in ferro's HTTP surface and are tested entirely in-process.

sub_area: frappe.local thread-local proxy / LocalProxy override correctness
rationale: Tests the Werkzeug LocalProxy threading behaviour of frappe.local; this is a Python runtime concern with no HTTP surface and no analogue in ferro's Rust codebase.

sub_area: mask_field_value utility: per-fieldtype masking patterns (Data, Link, Phone, Email, Date, Time, None/empty)
rationale: Calls the Python mask_field_value() utility function directly; ferro does not implement field masking (mask=1 DocField attribute), so this pure utility test is irrelevant to ferro.

sub_area: End-to-end field masking: get_doc, apply_fieldlevel_read_permissions, db.get_list masking for non-admin, _restore_masked_fields_from_db, mask permission property
rationale: Tests the Python document lifecycle for field masking (mask=1 DocField); ferro has no concept of field-level masking in its ORM layer, so these behaviors are intentionally absent and not tested over HTTP.

sub_area: Masked Link field + User Permissions interaction: read and save without permission error
rationale: Regression test for masked Link field + user-permission gating in the Python document layer; ferro does not implement field masking so this entire class is out of scope for the pure-Rust build.

sub_area: get_fetch_values, get_permitted_fields (per user/role, core doctypes, child tables), is_default_field
rationale: Tests in-process Python model utilities; get_permitted_fields encodes permission-filtered field lists that ferro's auth.rs/meta.rs must replicate for correct ORM masking, but the Python functions themselves are not exposed over HTTP by ferro directly.

sub_area: export_module_json, export_customizations (with module filter), sync_customizations, trim_table for dev-mode doctype export/sync
rationale: Tests developer-mode tooling for exporting doctype JSON and customizations to disk; ferro has no module export/sync capability and this is firmly out of scope for the REST runtime.

sub_area: frappe.monitor: request/job tracing to Redis, flush to log file, trace_id injection into SQL
rationale: Tests the Python monitor/tracing subsystem that writes to Redis and log files; ferro has no equivalent monitoring pipeline (its realtime.rs is an in-process socket.io replacement, not a request monitor), so this is out of scope.

sub_area: autoname rules: field, format (date parts, consecutive week, expression), hash, UUID v7, naming_series prefix/validation, revert_series, cancelled/amended naming, custom parser hook, append_number_if_name_exists
rationale: Naming is a core contract ferro reimplements in naming.rs (naming_series, field:, format:, hash, expression); these in-process tests encode the exact behaviors ferro must replicate when generating names on insert — ferro covers common patterns but UUID v7 and custom parser hooks are gaps.

sub_area: NestedSet tree: lft/rgt integrity, move, delete, rebuild_tree, merge, recursion guard, descendants-of filter, disabled records in treeview
rationale: NestedSet is a Python-level DocType feature (lft/rgt tree maintenance on save/delete) with no direct ferro analogue; ferro's ORM does not implement tree maintenance hooks, so these tests are out of scope for the pure-Rust build.

sub_area: not_nullable DocField: default empty string on insert, DDL column constraint change via DocType save
rationale: Tests the not_nullable DocField attribute's effect on DB schema (DDL) and insert default values; ferro's schema.rs handles DDL during install/migrate but not_nullable column semantics at runtime insert are not explicitly implemented, so partial coverage at best.
